newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-THOMAS HITS TWO HOMERS AS WHITE SOX BEAT RED SOX 10-5.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-THOMAS HITS TWO HOMERS AS WHITE SOX BEAT RED SOX 10-5.

text.p: Red-hot Frank Thomas homered twice and drove in five runs as the Chicago White Sox extended their season-high winning streak to six games with a 10-5 victory over the plummeting Boston Red Sox on Wednesday.
In the second inning, Thomas and Albert Belle hit back-to-back homers for the first time, giving the White Sox a 7-1 lead. Belle's home run extended his hitting streak to 17 games.
Chris Hammond (1-3) was tagged for seven runs and eight hits in four innings for Boston.

"I'm not doing anything special, I'm just trying to hit the ball hard," Thomas said. "I'm trying to see the ball better and go deeper in the count and I can do that because I have good hitters behind me."

In Baltimore, Scott Erickson scattered four hits over 7 2/3 scoreless innings and Rafael Palmeiro's first-inning homer accounted for all the offence as the Baltimore Orioles blanked the Detroit Tigers 2-0 for their fifth consecutive victory.

Erickson (8-1), who has won six consecutive starts, became the American League's second eight-game winner, joining teammate Jimmy Key. In the six-game winning streak, Erickson has allowed only nine earned runs over 46 innings for an ERA of 1.57.

In Cleveland, Orel Hershiser and three relievers combined on a six-hitter, and Jim Thome scored the game's only run on a double steal as the Cleveland Indians won their fourth straight game by edging the Kansas City Royals, 1-0.
Hershiser (4-2) walked three and struck out three in 7-1/3 innings to snap his two-game losing streak.
Royals starter Kevin Appier tossed a two-hitter but took his third loss in his last four decisions. He struck out seven and walked eight.

In Milwaukee, Ben McDonald pitched 5-2/3 innings and Dave Nilsson's two-run single capped a four-run second inning as the Milwaukee Brewers ended a seven-game losing streak with a 5-4 victory over the Minnesota Twins.
McDonald (5-3) allowed four runs -- three earned -- and eight hits with no walks and five strikeouts.
Bob Wickman pitched 2-1/3 hitless innings, while Doug Jones worked a 1-2-3 ninth to collect his 10th save and 252nd of his career, tying him with Dave Righetti for 10th place on the all-time list.

In New York, Roger Clemens allowed four hits and struck out 12 in eight innings for his 200th career win, and Ed Sprague belted a three-run homer as the Toronto Blue Jays completed a two-game sweep of the New York Yankees with a 4-1 victory.
Clemens (8-0) walked three and lowered his ERA to 1.86 with his 71st career game with 10 or more strikeouts.
At Texas, Geronimo Berroa homered and drove in three runs as the Oakland Athletics halted their four-game losing streak and split of their two-game series with a 7-3 victory over the Texas Rangers.
Dave Telgheder gave up three runs in 7-1/3 innings to earn the victory. Oakland had dropped 11 of its previous 13 games.
Julio Santana (2-1) was tagged for six runs -- four earned -- and six hits with two walks in 4 1/3 innings.
At Anaheim, Gary DiSarcina matched career highs with four hits and four RBI and the Anaheim Angels had their biggest offensive output since 1995 in an 18-3 rout over the Seattle Mariners.
Anaheim's 18 runs were the most runs it scored 20 runs at Texas on June 29th, 1995. DiSarcina went 4-for-6 with two doubles and two runs scored for the Angels, who won for the ninth time in 10 games.
Garrett Anderson and Jim Edmonds each had three hits to extend hitting streaks. Anderson has hit in his last 16 games, while Edmonds has a 10-game streak.
